description: The divine Name — the essential Word/identity of the Waheguru whose recitation liberates the soul from the cycle of rebirth.
caveats: ਨਾਇ can mean 'bathing' in a few contexts (e.g. ਨਾਇ ਕਰੀ = 'what good is bathing'); the vast majority of its 169 occurrences carry the sense 'in/with the Name'. ਨਾਮਾ is predominantly 'hari naama' (divine Name); one occurrence refers to Bhagat Namdev.

description: Wondrous Enlightener (Waheguru) — the primary Sikh epithet for the Divine, combining wonder (vāh) and the primal Guru.
caveats: ਵਾਹੁ (156) is the exclamation 'wonderful/wondrous' that seeds the Vahiguru mantra; only the 13 instances of ਵਾਹਿਗੁਰੂ and 3 of ਵਾਹਗੁਰੂ are the explicit compound name. ਵਾਹਿ (4) appears in exclamatory praise lines.

description: Divine Command/Order — the sovereign will of the Creator by which all creation exists, moves, and is judged.
caveats: ਹੁਕਮਾਵੈ is rare (1 occurrence) but confirmed in corpus.

description: The Timeless / Eternal (Akāl) — the Divine beyond time and death; the 'Undying' of the Mool Mantar (ਅਕਾਲ ਮੂਰਤਿ).
caveats: Split out from the former 'akal_kaal' (audit 2026-06-19): only the ਅਕਾਲ forms (the Eternal) belong here (~92% on-theme). The ਕਾਲ death/time forms moved to the separate 'kaal' concept so the Eternal is no longer conflated with mortality.

description: Time, Death & Mortality (Kāl) — the Messenger of Death (Jam-kāl), the last moment (ਅੰਤਿ ਕਾਲਿ), and the dark age (ਕਲਿ ਕਾਲ); the temporal/mortal pole that the soul transcends through the Name.
caveats: Split out from the former 'akal_kaal' (audit 2026-06-19): these forms overwhelmingly denote death and temporal idioms, NOT the Eternal. Excluded false friends: ਕਾਲਾ (20), ਕਾਲੀ (11), ਕਾਲੇ (18) = the colour 'black'. The Eternal (ਅਕਾਲ) is now the separate 'akal' concept.

description: The Creator — names and verbal forms pointing to God as the sole maker and sustainer of all creation.
caveats: ਕਰਤੇ/ਕਰਤੈ are oblique/vocative of ਕਰਤਾ and consistently mean 'of/O Creator'. ਸਿਰਜਨਹਾਰ forms mean 'the one who created/creates' and are included as a near-synonym cluster.

description: The True Guru — the divine preceptor (both as the historical Sikh Gurus and as the eternal inner illuminator) who connects the seeker to the Divine Name.
caveats: ਗੁਰ (3135) is the most frequent form and appears in numerous compounds (e.g. ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ, ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ); here only the standalone ਗੁਰ is counted. The Satguru forms are the explicit 'True Guru' epithet and the plain Gur/Guru forms are overlapping.

description: The Divine Word/Hymn — the living utterance of the Guru, both the scriptural compositions and the cosmic vibration of Truth that permeates creation.
caveats: ਸ਼ਬਦ (with nukta) returns 0 hits — the corpus uses ਸਬਦ without nukta throughout. ਸਬਦਹੁ also returns 0.

description: Nectar of Immortality — the ambrosial essence of the divine Name that, when imbibed through naam-simran, grants liberation from death and rebirth.
caveats: ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੈ returns 0; the dative/locative form does not appear. ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੋ (2) is very rare but confirmed.

description: One Universal Creator (Ik Oankaar) — the foundational declaration of the singular, indivisible, all-pervading Divine Reality that opens the Japji and the entire scripture.
caveats: ੴ (111) is the Mool Mantar symbol itself. ਓਅੰਕਾਰੁ returns 0 in word_freq (the form ਓਅੰ=3, ਓਅੰਕਾਰ=2, ਓਅੰਕਾਰਿ=10 are present). ਏਕੰਕਾਰੁ=25 is a synonym epithet. ਇਕੁ/ਇਕਿ/ਇਕੋ are the ik- root forms ('one/only one') distinct from the ਏਕੁ/ਏਕ set but semantically unified here.

description: Remembrance/Meditation — the practice of continuously contemplating and reciting the divine Name, encompassing simran (remembrance), bhajan (devotional singing), jap (repetition), dhyaan (ਧਿਆਨ, focused meditation) and aradhana (ਅਰਾਧਿ/ਆਰਾਧਿ, adoring contemplation).
caveats: ਜਪੁ/ਜਪਿ/ਜਾਪੁ overlap with naam-recitation and are included. ADDED (audit 2026-06-19): the ਧਿਆਨ/dhyaan family (ਧਿਆਇਆ, ਧਿਆਇ, ਧਿਆਏ, ਧਿਆਵੈ, ਧਿਆਵਹੁ, ਧਿਆਈ, ਧਿਆਨੁ, ਧਿਆਨ), the ਅਰਾਧਿ/ਆਰਾਧਿ adoration forms, and ਜਪੀਐ — ~600+ explicit 'meditate' lines that were previously untagged (a large recall gap). ਜਾਪੈ was considered but EXCLUDED — it is a homograph also meaning 'appears / is perceived'. ਭਜਿ is mildly dual (meditate vs. 'run to the Sanctuary').

description: Praise and Glorification — the laudation of God's qualities and greatness through hymn, speech, and devoted contemplation; together these terms express the Gurbani ethic of perpetual praise.
caveats: ਸਾਲਾਹੁ returns 0 (the imperative form ਸਾਲਾਹਿ=23 is the attested form). ਵਡਿਆਈ (320) is the most common single term in this cluster, meaning 'greatness/glory'.

description: Sacred Utterance/Scripture — the Guru's divine speech, both the body of Gurbani compositions and the spiritual sound-current that is the Guru's essential form.
caveats: ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ (33) is the compound 'Guru's Bani'; ਗੁਰਬਾਣਿ returns 0. Many more occurrences of ਬਾਣੀ exist within compounds (e.g. ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ already counted separately) — the standalone ਬਾਣੀ (340) is the primary form.

description: The Blessed Vision — beholding God or the Guru in His divine form; the transformative spiritual 'seeing' that grants liberation and peace.
caveats: ਦੀਦਾਰੁ/ਦੀਦਾਰ/ਦੀਦਾਰਿ are the Farsi-rooted equivalents of ਦਰਸਨ and are included as near-synonyms in this cluster.

description: The Lotus Feet — the sacred feet of the Guru/God as a devotional focus and metaphor for humble surrender, refuge, and grace.
caveats: ਚਰਣਾਰਬਿੰਦ (8) = 'lotus-feet' compound. ਪਗ/ਪਗਿ/ਪੈਰ/ਪੈਰੀ are synonymous 'feet' terms and almost always appear in devotional surrender contexts (ਗੁਰ ਕੀ ਪੈਰੀ ਪਾਹਿ). ਪਾਇ (393) was considered but excluded as too ambiguous ('to receive/attain' vs. 'at the feet'). ਚਰਣੈ returns 0.

description: Divine Will/Pleasure — joyful, unconditional acceptance of whatever the Waheguru wills; the spiritual stance of complete surrender to God's pleasure (bhana mannana).
caveats: ਭਾਵੈ ('as it pleases Thee') is the verbal root of ਭਾਣਾ and clearly denotes divine will in context. ਰਜਾਇ/ਰਜਾਈ are the Farsi/Arabic-rooted equivalents (razā = divine pleasure). ਭਾਉ (love/devotion) was considered but is a distinct concept and excluded. ਰਜ਼ਾ (with nukta) returns 0.
